$comment: Allowlist for scripts/check-scan-findings.mjs, the gate over the scanners that run
outside the JS test suite: Trivy image and IaC scans, and the ZAP baseline, in
The grammar is the same as scripts/semgrep-allowlist.json on purpose. A finding at
or above the job's severity floor with no entry fails CI. An entry past its expiry
fails CI even though the finding still matches, so an acceptance cannot outlive the
triage that justified it. An entry that matches nothing fails CI as stale.
"scanner" is "trivy" or "zap" and scopes the entry to one report, so a ZAP alert
can never excuse a Trivy CVE that happens to share its number. Omit "locations"
to accept a finding wherever it appears; each value is matched as a substring of the
finding's location, which is "<target>:<package>@<version>" for a Trivy
vulnerability, the scanned path for a misconfiguration, and a URL for a ZAP alert.
A ZAP alert becomes one finding per URL it lists, and every one of them has to match.
Its "id" is the alert reference, such as 10055-4, not the plugin id: plugin 10055
alone raises a dozen different Content-Security-Policy alerts, and accepting one must
not accept the rest. ZAP lists only five URLs for an alert it marks systemic, so an
entry scoped by "locations" vouches for the URLs the report shows and no others.

entries.reason: img-src admits any https: origin, the only directive ZAP reports as unbounded. Chat renders images whose host is decided at runtime by a model or a search provider: markdown images (MarkdownImage in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx accepts any http or https source) and the favicons search results carry (WebSearchCard.tsx, CitationChip.tsx, ResearchPanel.tsx). A host list would break them. Removing the wildcard needs a same-origin image proxy for those paths, the pattern MCP directory icons and place photos already use.

style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' because a nonce covers style elements, not style attributes: apps/web and packages/ui render about 2,300 React style props across 215 components, and Clerk documents 'unsafe-inline' as required for its components to inject their styles (clerk.com/docs/guides/secure/best-practices/csp-headers, read 2026-10-01). script-src stays nonce-only, which scripts/check-security-response-headers.mjs enforces. The exemption is disclosed on /security and pinned by apps/web/app/trust/posture-claims.test.ts.

Both flagged tags are Clerk's, served from its Frontend API host: @clerk/nextjs renders clerk-js (/npm/@clerk/clerk-js@6/dist/clerk.browser.js) and preloads @clerk/ui (/npm/@clerk/ui@1/dist/ui.browser.js) with no integrity attribute. Each URL names a major version Clerk updates in place, so no fixed hash can match it. First-party scripts are same-origin and outside this alert. Removing the CDN load means bundling @clerk/clerk-js and @clerk/ui into the build, a dependency change.
